summary: Marielle Harrison works in religious and Buddhist studies. A doctoral student at the University of Chicago (attested 2026), she served as an HCBSS Postdoctoral Fellow Lecturer in the Department of Religious Studies at Stanford University (attested 2026).

Marina Illich is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University in 2006, supervised by Robert A. F. Thurman, with Ryuichi Abe, Angela Zito, and John Stratton Hawley as teachers, and Chopathar Wayemache as mentor.

Mario D'Amato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He held posts at Hampshire College (attested 2001) and Rollins College as an assistant professor.

Mario Poceski specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning his PhD from UCLA in 2000 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., he taught at the University of Iowa (2001) and the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

Mario Praz (1896–1982) studied at the University of Bologna (~1914–1918) and the University of Florence (~1918–1920). He held academic posts at the University of Manchester (~1932–1934) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1934–1966).
Marion L. Matics is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Matics studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, and was taught by Robert A. Fowkes.

Marion Meyer (born 1954) is a historian and archaeologist. She held appointments at the German Archaeological Institute (1984–1985), the University of Florida (1996), the University of Bonn (~1997–2003), and the University of Vienna (~2003–2020).

Mark A. Nathan works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. His career includes posts at Kangwon National University, UCLA, and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

Mark Allon, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his PhD from Cambridge (~1989–1994) under K. R. Norman. He worked at SOAS (~1994–1998) before joining the University of Sydney, where he served as department chair (attested 2015–2017).

Mark Csikszentmihalyi (born 1964) is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He served as Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2004) and became Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at UC Berkeley around 2004.

Mark D. Griffiths (born 1966) earned a BSc from the University of Bradford and a PhD from the University of Exeter (1988–1990). He lectured at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) and became Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).

Mark Elliott specializes in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He served as professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1993–2003) and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University around 2003.

Mark Jan Dresden (1911–1986) was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Amsterdam and Utrecht, and under Jan Gonda, Harold Walter Bailey, and Walter Bruno Henning, before teaching at the University of Pennsylvania (1949–1977).

Mark Juergensmeyer (born 1940) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at Illinois, Union Theological Seminary, Columbia, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1974), he held professorships at UC Santa Barbara (~1993) and Claremont McKenna College (~2017).

Mark L. Blum specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held faculty posts at the State University of New York (attested 2005) and University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2006), later becoming Professor and Shinjo Ito Distinguished Chair at UC Berkeley (attested 2026).
Mark Owen is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral work under the supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.
Mark Rowe is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has served as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at McMaster University (attested 2015, 2026).

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (1951–2025) was a scholar of Indology and religion. He studied at BHU, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Oxford (DPhil ~1974–1979 under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson), while also studying under traditional teachers including Swami Lakshman Joo.

Mark Siderits (born 1946) is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served on the faculty at Illinois State University (~1979–2008) and later at Seoul National University (~2008–2014).

Mark Singleton (born 1969) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge, studying under Elizabeth De Michelis. He served as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).
